title: Dimensionless frequency-loop integral
description: For ordinary frequency f measured in hertz and elapsed time t measured in seconds, the integral of f dt is a dimensionless cycle count. Its dimensionlessness does not by itself establish invariance under arbitrary changes of path or parameterization.
definitions: f is ordinary frequency in hertz (s^-1), not angular frequency.
t is physical time measured in seconds.
Omega is the number of cycles accumulated over the explicitly specified integration domain.
equations: m_E = E / c^2 = h f / c^2 = k f
assumptions: The closed integration domain C and its physical-time parameterization are specified.
The frequency-mass relation applies to the mass equivalent of energy E = h f; it does not assign rest mass to a photon or an arbitrary oscillator.
With h in J s and c in m s^-1, k has units kg s and k f has units kg.
mechanism: The dimensionless result follows from multiplying ordinary frequency (s^-1) by physical time (s) and integrating over a specified domain. The relation m_E = k f is the algebraic composition of E = h f and E = m_E c^2.
primary_sources: SI Brochure, ninth edition: hertz and second
2019 SI definition of the Planck constant h
Einstein (1905), inertia of energy, E = m c^2
falsification_conditions: Dimensional analysis of the declared f and t units does not yield a dimensionless cycle count.
The stated mass-equivalent composition fails when E = h f and m_E = E/c^2 are applied within their declared domain.
confusion_guard: A dimensionless integral is not automatically an invariant. The closed-loop notation requires a specified domain, and integer quantization is a separate symbolic postulate recorded independently.
